source_caption:
Bullet Train (2022), directed by David Leitch, was designed to be a fast, stylish action film where humor and chaos move at the same speed as the train itself. Brad Pitt was cast as Ladybug, an unlucky assassin trying to finish one simple job while avoiding violence, which made the role a fun change from his more serious action characters. Pitt even performed many of his own stunts, something the director encouraged to keep the action feeling more physical and real.

The film is based on the Japanese novel Maria Beetle by Kotaro Isaka, and much of the movie takes place on a high speed train inspired by Japan’s famous Shinkansen system. To create the tight, fast moving atmosphere, most of the train interiors were built as detailed sets, allowing the camera to move freely and capture the chaotic fights happening in narrow spaces.

One interesting detail is that several characters were written with strong, distinct personalities to make the ensemble feel unpredictable. The dynamic between the twin assassins Lemon and Tangerine, played by Brian Tyree Henry and Aaron Taylor-Johnson, became a fan favorite, especially because of Lemon’s obsession with Thomas the Tank Engine references throughout the film.

Director David Leitch, who previously worked as a stunt coordinator, focused heavily on choreography, blending comedy with fast paced action. The result is a film that doesn’t take itself too seriously, mixing colorful visuals, sudden twists, and constant momentum into a wild ride that rarely slows down.

source_details.synopsis: Bullet Train is a 2022 American action comedy film directed by David Leitch. Based on the 2010 Japanese novel by Kōtarō Isaka, it centers around a group of assassins on a Japanese high-speed train who end up in conflict with each other. The ensemble cast consists of Brad Pitt, Joey King, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Brian Tyree Henry, Andrew Koji, Hiroyuki Sanada, Michael Shannon, Bad Bunny, and Sandra Bullock. Principal photography began in Los Angeles in November 2020 and concluded in March 2021 amid the COVID-19 pandemic.
